newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Crew safe,but beer cargo lost as ship sinks off HK.
newsitem.headline: Crew safe,but beer cargo lost as ship sinks off HK.

text.p: A Chinese cargo ship capsized off western Hong Kong and hurled nearly half a million cans of beer into the ocean, but all 10 crew members were saved, reports said on Thursday.
The steel-hulled vessel Hengtong 320, sank on Wednesday, LLP Ltd of London, formerly an associate company of Lloyds, said in a statement. A spokesman added there were no immediate details.
But a Hong Kong newspaper said the 700-tonne ship lost its cargo of 480,000 cans of beer when it went down in heavy seas in the early hours of Wednesday.
The coaster was sailing from Zhaoqing in China's southern Guangdong province to Nanjing, provincial capital of Jiangsu, the Tin Tin Daily News said.
The crew from Fujian province, who bought the ship for a total of about 600,000 yuan (US$72,300), were plucked out of the ocean by a rescue patrol, the newspaper said. None needed hospital treatment.
Many people in Hong Kong and China are preparing to celebrate ahead of July 1 when China regains control of the British territory, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
